destruction of bony and cartilaginous septum
Typical saddle-nose deformities with columellar retraction and nasal collapse.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels ((a), (b)). (a): CT scan demonstrates midline destruction of bone and cartilage, characteristic of cocaine-induced midline destructive lesion. (b): Clinical photograph showing typical saddle-nose deformity, a hallmark of this condition.
panels.attribution_text: Di Cosola et al. Cocaine-Induced Midline Destructive Lesions (CIMDL): A Real Challenge in Diagnosis.. International journal of environmental research and public health 2021. doi:10.3390/ijerph18157831. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: (a) Case 5. Destruction of bony and cartilaginous septum revealed by CT scan. (b) Typical saddle-nose deformities with columellar retraction and nasal collapse.
in_text_mentions: In two cases, the chronic cocaine inhalation caused a complete erosion of hard palate extended until the soft palate, with destruction of bony and cartilaginous septum, ethmoidal cells, turbinates and medial maxillary sinus walls, revealed by CT scan (Figure 2a). The nasal involvement resulted in typical saddle-nose deformities with columellar retraction and nasal collapse (Figure 2b).
